summary: Night's hero extras, all four built: (1) the bar clock in Night draws HH:MM as seven-segment bars (crt_qt.Screen.seven_segment) in her phosphor over faint unlit 88:88, the date small under it in the mono face; Day, Pencil and Indigo unchanged. (2) Her new lines in her panel type out behind a block cursor at 600 characters a second (never over 0.8 s), with the characters lit in the last AFTERGLOW_MS glowing behind it. A click shows the line whole. It is instant under Reduce motion, with CRT effects Off and outside Night. A card (a line with a button) is always shown whole. The line's height is reserved and the thread follows the cursor. (3) Peak marks: in Night the equalizer's peak dots hold the highest value for 2.5 s, then fall 0.25 of the scale a second; the peak is the tokens' 'peak' (amber in Duo); the Night word meters get a slim green bar with an amber peak tick. (4) Night: Paper, a fourth phosphor (#c9d1d3, steps 220/195/125) under View > Appearance; every text pair is 4.5:1 or more.
existing_tests_changed: tests_integrated/test_night_phosphor.py Duo.test_duo_is_the_default_night_and_amber_and_green_stay_choices: np_.PHOSPHORS now has a fourth entry ('paper', 'Night: Paper'), which item 4 asks for
decisions: Clock colour is the tokens' kas_text: amber in Duo and Amber; Green's and Paper's clocks are their own phosphor, so the single phosphors stay one hue. The plan names amber for every Night; this keeps N1's one-hue rule.
Unlit 88:88 bars under the clock at 26/255 of the phosphor, like an LED clock.

Type-out runs in every Night phosphor when crt_fx has afterglow (Night, CRT effects not Off, no Reduce motion). The cursor is in kas_text. The afterglow is three fading bands of the phosphor behind the cursor over AFTERGLOW_MS.
A card is a bubble with a button, or with more than its words, checked at say() and on every tick, because buttons are added after say() returns.
Peak hold 2.5 s, fall 0.25 of the scale a second. Applied in every Night, so Day's equalizer is unchanged. The colour is the tokens' 'peak', so amber shows only in Duo.

Night's foot meters are words only, so their peak mark is a 2 px bar of the reading (green, or amber with the existing hot mark) with a 2x6 px amber tick under the words. They repaint on each reading, so the fall steps once a reading.
Paper's shares 220/195/125 (secondary/tertiary/disabled), measured by the NIGHT_PAIRS test; colour_vision NIGHT_CLOSE['paper'] is the same as Amber's (one hue: every pair is told by word or shape).
findings_for_the_coordinator: In Night: Duo her conversation bubbles (shell2.Bubble, SlateTheirs) draw her words in green #33ff66, not amber. Measured in the frame: palette foreground #33ff66, no stylesheet. N1duo says Kas's words are amber. This predates HX; HX's cursor is amber and the words keep the bubble's colour.
The bar stands only in an X session. The frame was composed from the offscreen window plus a Bar built directly, at 1920x1200.
not_done: No 1366x768 frame (the slice asked for the one 1920x1200 frame).
No tier or full-suite run (by the rules).
Nothing ran on the owner's ThinkPad.
release_note: Night gets its hero touches. The bar's clock is an LED desk clock in seven-segment digits. Kas's new lines type out behind her block cursor, and a click shows a line at once; under Reduce motion or with CRT effects Off they appear whole, as do her cards. The activity bars and meters keep an amber peak mark that holds for a moment and then falls. A fourth Night, Night: Paper, is a white-phosphor terminal in paper-white grey.
